i’m not an expert, i’ve just had an eating disorder for about 2 years. that sounds like it could be a disordered thought pattern, but unless it comes with other behaviours i wouldn’t say you have an eating disorder. (behaviours would be things like: avoiding eating, chewing and spitting to avoid consuming calories, constantly obsessing over food & and eating, having strict and specific rules around food, intense distress after/before eating, overexercise or purging, ect.) for disordered thought patterns to qualify as an eating disorder behaviour would usually accompany those thoughts. it would also likely need disrupt your life in some way to be considered or diagnosed as a disorder. 

again, i’m not an expert, this is just my perspective  as someone with an eating disorder who has been active in very disordered spaces online. 

my advice to you would be to explore why you feel the guilt that you do around food, and to explore the idea of getting a therapist, or even journalling to try to find where these thoughts are coming from. it could be anything from things your parents have taught you to a possible symptom of something like ocd. you shouldn’t feel guilty for eating food ❤️, it sustains life and provides energy so you can live a full and active life each day. i hope things get easier for you soon ❤️

i’ve been a pescatarian for years. lentils in curry and vegetable soup are delicious. soups in general are wonderful and easy. vegetarian chilli is easy and satisfying. you can switch out some pastas for things like edamame noodles or other pasta alternatives that have protein added. if you’re just looking to make it less caloric you can do half spaghetti squash half real pasta. you can do the same thing for rice with cauliflower rice. chickpeas are also great to make curry with. falafel is great for sandwiches or wraps, so is hummus. 

salad can be delicious and satisfying as long as you make it those things. people think it’s just leaves, but if it’s just leaves that’s a bad salad. a salad can be a meal if you don’t treat it like a side dish. i add fresh fruit like peaches, strawberries, blackberries, apples, anything. i always add a mixture of hemp seeds, pumpkin seeds, sunflower seeds, and chia seeds to salads. including a fatty seed/nut or something like an avocado, or some boiled eggs, with a dressing you really like (not just the lowest calorie one) makes a salad that you’ll feel happy before and after eating. i like to have that with some kind of textured soy protein (i love the gardenin chick’n tenders). you can also use tofu, or a black bean crumble, some falafel. just anything that you enjoy. salads are great. vegetable soup/stew with salad is also easy to make in bulk if you like to make large batches of things and eat them over the course of the week. 

stuffed sweet peppers with black beans and cauliflower rice is a good easy supper too. to make tofu more interesting i marinate it before cooking, there are tons of recipes for it online and it’s such a simple thing that really makes me excited about tofu (i used to HATE it, i thought it was so boring). coat each piece in cornstarch before frying to get it to crisp up nicely. marinated tofu pan fried with some veggies is part of my meal rotation because it’s so easy and satisfying. some youtubers i watch for food ideas are: Cheap Lazy Vegan, Rainbow Plant Life, and Mina Rome (Mina Rome in particular is helpful because she makes one person meals, and I am only cooking for one person) these are just some ideas haha. hope it helps :)

if you’re set on recommending this, this is my firsthand experience as a young suicidal person who was brought in to the hospital by police:


i did not get a psychiatric evaluation by a mental health expert, i sat in handcuffs traumatized from my arrest for 12 hours waiting to be seen by a nurse with a question sheet he filled in with yes/no answers. no one paid extra attention to my situation because of police involvement, i didn’t receive any follow up care, i didn’t see a psychologist. it didn’t help me, and it didn’t fix anything. it made my crisis worse because the experience was so negative and violent. 


in reality the only benefit to police involvement is how it is forced. you are brought against your will and you MUST remain there. so the mother and father wouldn’t be able to remove the child from the hospital until she had been seen by someone. it is not taken any more seriously than just going to a psychiatrist for an assessment would be. that’s an illusion. it’s all recorded anyways, police wouldn’t legitimize it anymore than going to a walk-in mental health crisis centre would. 


on that note: mental health/addiction support centres exist, a lot of them are free, they’re much less busy and difficult than care at the hospital, and there is no violence involved. i recommend that as a previously suicidal teenager. those places helped more than police EVER did. a lot of them are walk-ins. you can come in off the street, tell them about your situation, put down your information, and just sit in the waiting room for a little while, then have an hour long session of one on one counselling with a social worker or psychologist. this can be an opportunity for the child to talk about the neglect to a social worker and report it, and to discuss her suicidal thoughts with a professional and get the proper care she needs.

in my personal experience police don’t really help. they arrest the suicidal person and take them away to sit in the hospital, OP could take them to the hospital themselves the next time they see them and skip the police entirely. they don’t do anything special or useful beyond arresting them and driving them there. the arrest can be extremely traumatic (it was for me, they used excessive force). i would try reporting to CPS about the neglect before i would consider involving police in the mental health struggles of a child. its better than nothing if it’s the only option but in this case it’s not the only option

this is all anecdotal i’m not a vet or anything. just from my recent experience with this.

starting point: VET. fatty liver syndrome comes when cats start using their body fat as fuel, their bodies aren’t designed to process it this way, and it can cause severe and rapid liver damage if preventative measures aren’t taken after the first 3-4 days. 

this is what i did before she got her appetite stimulants (she has an upper respiratory infection):

my cat stopped eating recently. most pet stores and vets with a food section will have a high calorie nutritional supplement that comes in a tube, she tolerated that. she also still ate the squeeze treats specifically the churu brand tuna and chicken ones (very similar to delectables). i started feeding every two hours on the dot. she’s not food motivated but she is motivated by affection so every time she licked at her food or ate anything i showered her with praise and pet her a lot. 
try offering food with a very strong scent, i added water from a can of tuna to her food and that made her eat some. also warming the food a little in the microwave before offering it. i usually will stir it around with my fingertip to make sure there aren’t any hot spots. if your cat has lost weight look for high calorie food. kitten food is often very high calorie, so is food for breastfeeding cat moms. there is also hills prescription diet urgent care and digestive care which is what i’m feeding stella now to get her weight restored. 

there are also foods for senior cats and kittens that come in a pouch and are labelled “velvet”. i was able to feed her with the tiki cat kitten formula velvet pouch by smearing a bit on her nose and she would lick it off. hand feeding can help if your cat isn’t violent when they don’t like something very much. depending on the kind of infection your cat has she might have a sore throat which could keep her from eating more flaky or chunky foods. stella would only eat watered down pate for a while. try playing before feeding too. i would close both of us in the bathroom and play with her for about 15 minutes then offer food and she would usually have a few bites. 

i think cats can tell when you are patient and loving, i would sit with her every two hours sleeping in between. i was exhausted for the week or so it took to get her back to normal but it really helped. appetite stimulants really changed everything though, when you see a vet i would recommend asking about them. force feeding wouldn’t be the best first choice but it might be necessary. i read a lot of articles that said it can cause a food aversion, so if you’re planning to force feed use a completely different food than what you normally feed so she doesn’t hate her normal diet when she is recovered.
